New Features: - Add public const-safe builders for all supported field types, including JSON, with type-specific options and preserved literal inference. - Support reusable field definitions that retain literal names, enum members, defaults, metadata, nullability, and index-name validation. Bug Fixes: - Align resource record nullability with declared schema defaults and nullable fields. - Normalize persisted nulls for non-nullable fields to absent values in server and client query results. - Ensure replace mutations clear omitted fields consistently while preserving nullable defaults. - Validate date field bounds and date defaults during schema and mutation validation. Enhancements: - Improve schema and field type inference guidance, including widening pitfalls and the use of satisfies or builders. - Expose date-bound conversion and record normalization utilities through the core package. Documentation: - Document const-safe field builders, inference preservation, JSON fields, replace clearing semantics, and the scope of runtime constraint enforcement. Tests: - Add runtime and compile-time coverage for field builders, reusable fields, type inference, validation, date bounds, nullability, replace clearing, and normalized query results. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds const-safe field builders to `@datafn/core` so reusable fields keep literal names, enums, and metadata without widening, and aligns `DatafnResourceRecord` nullability with runtime defaults. **New Features** - Adds `field.string`, `field.number`, `field.boolean`, `field.object`, `field.array`, `field.date`, `field.file`, and `field.json` builders. - Builders emit explicit `required: false` and `nullable: false` defaults when omitted and drop `default` when it is `undefined`. - Options are type-checked per field kind; invalid defaults, enums, bounds, unknown options, and overridden `name` or `type` fail compilation. - Exported `Datafn*FieldOptions` types are accepted in builder calls, and `field.date` supports `min`/`max` bounds. **Behavior Changes** - `DatafnResourceRecord` now adds `null` only when `nullable: true`, including when `nullable` is widened to `boolean`. - Replace clears omitted fields as `null` in storage — the only clear every adapter persists — and server and client read paths (including relation results) expose them as `undefined` again for non-nullable fields; nullable required fields may use a `null` default. - Date `min`/`max` bounds are enforced during mutations and validated at schema definition, which rejects non-finite, inverted, or out-of-range defaults. - Docs warn that annotating schemas as `DatafnSchema` or field arrays as `DatafnFieldSchema[]` widens literals; use `satisfies` or builders instead. Written for commit 090dbf4b84c98bd47c49db8a2b60fcf774955461. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added const-safe schema field builders for all supported field types, including JSON. - Added numeric minimum and maximum bounds for date fields. - Builders preserve literal types, metadata, defaults, and required/nullable settings. - **Bug Fixes** - Corrected nullable field typing, including widened nullable options. - Nullable required fields can explicitly contain `null`. - Replace operations reset omitted fields to defaults or `null`, while reads expose cleared non-nullable fields as `undefined`. - Date bounds are enforced during mutations. - **Documentation** - Expanded guidance for builders, defaults, validation, constraints, replacement, and nullability. External MCP servers can point the harness at a URL plus explicit credentials without constructing `McpFnServer` or `McpFnRegistry`. - add `authenticatedHttpTarget()` / `connectAuthenticatedHttpTarget()` for URL + headers, credentials, or an auth-provider adapter - add independently configured Claude- and ChatGPT-shaped authorization cases, hosted role-3 coverage, layer classification, and redacted JUnit artifacts - accept repeatable CLI `--header` / `--junit` on `test-target`, `inspect`, and authenticated `conformance` (loopback proxy) - add a non-McpFn official-SDK HTTP example and wire it into `npm run gate:mcpfn-release` - document remote targets, authenticated conformance, the official runner pin (`0.1.16`), and upgrade policy Package versions are intentionally unchanged so Skillplane can keep pinning the current published line until the next coordinated release. ## Validation - `npm run typecheck --workspace=@mcpfn/testing && npm run test --workspace=@mcpfn/testing` (39 passed) - `npm run test --workspace=@mcpfn/cli && npm run build --workspace=@mcpfn/cli` (14 passed) - `node scripts/test-mcpfn-external-server.mjs` (authenticated `test-target --header --junit`; unauthenticated run fails; API key redacted) Full `npm run gate:mcpfn-release` was not run in this agent (Playwright + official conformance + packed consumer). The dedicated McpFn Node 22 gate should run on this PR. ## Boundaries - targets `dev` - does not change Skillplane application code - does not add a second production client, PKCE, or authorization implementation - does not bump `@mcpfn/*` package versions Linear: MCP-1 ## Summary by Sourcery Enable transport-neutral regression and conformance testing for authenticated remote MCP servers without requiring McpFn server or registry types. New Features: - Add transport-neutral authenticated remote-target APIs for connecting to MCP endpoints by URL with headers, credentials, or auth-provider adapters. - Support repeatable CLI authentication headers and JUnit output for target testing, inspection, and authenticated official conformance. - Add independently configurable Claude- and ChatGPT-shaped authorization cases, hosted role-3 OAuth coverage, protocol-layer failure classification, and redacted machine-readable reports. - Provide a non-McpFn official-SDK HTTP server example and include its authenticated consumer path in the McpFn release gate. Bug Fixes: - Ensure unsupported OAuth token grants and authorization failures are surfaced with the appropriate protocol-layer diagnostics. Enhancements: - Reuse existing authentication and OAuth primitives for hosted authorization and remote-target testing without introducing a second client or authorization stack. - Document remote targets, authenticated conformance, official runner pinning, CI coverage, and upgrade policy. Build: - Extend the McpFn release gate to validate the external official-SDK HTTP example and packed consumer path. Documentation: - Document URL-based third-party MCP targets, authenticated CLI usage, redacted JUnit artifacts, conformance runner versioning, and release-gate coverage. Tests: - Add CLI validation for repeatable and malformed authentication headers. - Add remote authenticated target, named-host authorization, hosted role-3 PKCE, failure classification, redaction, and unsupported-grant tests. --- ## Summary by cubic External MCP servers can now be regression- and conformance-tested by URL plus explicit credentials without constructing `McpFnServer` or `McpFnRegistry`, completing the third-party consumer path for MCP-1. **New Features** - `authenticatedHttpTarget()` and `connectAuthenticatedHttpTarget()` accept a URL plus headers, credentials, or an auth-provider adapter. - CLI `test-target`, `inspect`, and `conformance` accept repeatable `--header` flags; `test` and `test-target` also accept `--junit`. - Added independently configured Claude- and ChatGPT-shaped authorization cases, hosted role-3 coverage, and protocol-layer failure classification. - Added a non-McpFn official-SDK HTTP example under `mcpfn/examples`, exercised by `npm run gate:mcpfn-release`. - Authenticated conformance binds a temporary loopback-only proxy that injects headers without printing them. - Official conformance pin is `OFFICIAL_CONFORMANCE_VERSION` (currently `0.1.16`); upgrade it only with a dedicated change. Package versions are intentionally unchanged so Skillplane can keep pinning the current published line until the next coordinated release. Written for commit e0cd1257f74386abee32993452321a0f2d44b325. Summary will update on new commits. item.stdout: {"baseRefOid":"f6a2b03ee97f227e0db270c3b929b8bd0695cef8","body":"## Linear [DATA-6 — Expose canonical structural resource-selector extraction](https://linear.app/21n/issue/DATA-6/expose-canonical-structural-resource-selector-extraction) ## Summary - add a versioned `@datafn/core` protocol API (`parseDatafnRequest`, `collectStructuralResourceSelectors`, `extractStructuralResourceSelectors`) that returns only protocol-level resource selectors - inspect documented selector positions for query, mutation, batch, transact, search, clone, pull, push, and reconcile — never recurse into records, filters, or other domain JSON - return normalized, deduplicated selectors for gateway routing and `authorize` plugins; share the action inventory with `@datafn/server` via `DataFnAction` - fail closed on unknown actions (`DFQL_UNSUPPORTED`), malformed selectors (`DFQL_INVALID`), and unsupported `protocolVersion` (`DATAFN_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION`) - document this API as the supported security-sensitive integration point ## Verification - `@datafn/core` selector conformance: 28/28 passed (`resource-selectors.test.ts`) - `@datafn/server` authorize preflight: 2/2 passed (`resource-selectors-preflight.test.ts`) - parser and extractor share fixtures so a new envelope cannot be accepted by one without the other - regression fixtures ignore application fields named `resource` / `resources` ## Rollout notes and limitations This PR does not define application authorization policy or choose a regional cell. Skillplane can replace its local structural extractor after the next `@datafn/core` / `@datafn/server` publish. ## Non-goals - Recursive JSON search - Changing the meaning of application fields named `resource` or `resources` - Tenant placement or cell selection ## Summary by Sourcery Expose canonical structural resource-selector extraction for safe gateway routing and authorization preflight. New Features: - Add a versioned protocol API for parsing DataFn requests and extracting normalized, deduplicated structural resource selectors across supported actions. Bug Fixes: - Prevent authorization and routing integrations from mistaking application fields named `resource` or `resources` for protocol selectors. - Fail closed for unknown actions, malformed selector positions, disallowed protocol-object keys, and unsupported protocol versions. Enhancements: - Share the canonical request-action inventory and selector definitions between `@datafn/core` and `@datafn/server`. Documentation: - Document structural selector extraction as the supported security-sensitive integration point for gateways and authorization plugins, including its coverage and error behavior. Tests: - Add core conformance coverage for all request actions, selector positions, normalization, deduplication, malformed inputs, protocol versions, and application-field regression cases. - Add server authorization preflight coverage using the canonical selector extractor. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a versioned protocol API in `@datafn/core` that extracts structural resource selectors from request envelopes, so gateways and `authorize` plugins stop recursively scanning request JSON for fields named `resource` or `resources`. The same action inventory now feeds `@datafn/server` through `DataFnAction`. **New Features** - `parseDatafnRequest`, `collectStructuralResourceSelectors`, and `extractStructuralResourceSelectors` inspect only protocol selector positions across query, mutation, batch, transact, search, clone, pull, push, and reconcile; application records and filter operands are ignored. - Selectors are normalized, deduplicated, and returned with the protocol version; omitting `protocolVersion` defaults to `"1"`. - Fails closed on unknown actions (`DFQL_UNSUPPORTED`), malformed selectors (`DFQL_INVALID`), and unsupported protocol versions (`DATAFN_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION`). - Re-exports the API from `@datafn/server` and shares the action inventory via `DataFnAction`; parser and extractor share fixtures so a new envelope shape cannot be accepted by one without the other. - Documents the API as the supported security-sensitive integration point in the request-authz, production-checklist, multi-region gateway, and reference docs. Written for commit 4eb55d039f969a4b37913aacf88fc85285c43fea. Summary will update on new commits. item.aggregated_output: {"baseRefOid":"f6a2b03ee97f227e0db270c3b929b8bd0695cef8","body":"## Linear [DATA-6 — Expose canonical structural resource-selector extraction](https://linear.app/21n/issue/DATA-6/expose-canonical-structural-resource-selector-extraction) ## Summary - add a versioned `@datafn/core` protocol API (`parseDatafnRequest`, `collectStructuralResourceSelectors`, `extractStructuralResourceSelectors`) that returns only protocol-level resource selectors - inspect documented selector positions for query, mutation, batch, transact, search, clone, pull, push, and reconcile — never recurse into records, filters, or other domain JSON - return normalized, deduplicated selectors for gateway routing and `authorize` plugins; share the action inventory with `@datafn/server` via `DataFnAction` - fail closed on unknown actions (`DFQL_UNSUPPORTED`), malformed selectors (`DFQL_INVALID`), and unsupported `protocolVersion` (`DATAFN_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION`) - document this API as the supported security-sensitive integration point ## Verification - `@datafn/core` selector conformance: 28/28 passed (`resource-selectors.test.ts`) - `@datafn/server` authorize preflight: 2/2 passed (`resource-selectors-preflight.test.ts`) - parser and extractor share fixtures so a new envelope cannot be accepted by one without the other - regression fixtures ignore application fields named `resource` / `resources` ## Rollout notes and limitations This PR does not define application authorization policy or choose a regional cell. Skillplane can replace its local structural extractor after the next `@datafn/core` / `@datafn/server` publish. ## Non-goals - Recursive JSON search - Changing the meaning of application fields named `resource` or `resources` - Tenant placement or cell selection ## Summary by Sourcery Expose canonical structural resource-selector extraction for safe gateway routing and authorization preflight. New Features: - Add a versioned protocol API for parsing DataFn requests and extracting normalized, deduplicated structural resource selectors across supported actions. Bug Fixes: - Prevent authorization and routing integrations from mistaking application fields named `resource` or `resources` for protocol selectors. - Fail closed for unknown actions, malformed selector positions, disallowed protocol-object keys, and unsupported protocol versions. Enhancements: - Share the canonical request-action inventory and selector definitions between `@datafn/core` and `@datafn/server`. Documentation: - Document structural selector extraction as the supported security-sensitive integration point for gateways and authorization plugins, including its coverage and error behavior. Tests: - Add core conformance coverage for all request actions, selector positions, normalization, deduplication, malformed inputs, protocol versions, and application-field regression cases. - Add server authorization preflight coverage using the canonical selector extractor. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a versioned protocol API in `@datafn/core` that extracts structural resource selectors from request envelopes, so gateways and `authorize` plugins stop recursively scanning request JSON for fields named `resource` or `resources`. The same action inventory now feeds `@datafn/server` through `DataFnAction`. **New Features** - `parseDatafnRequest`, `collectStructuralResourceSelectors`, and `extractStructuralResourceSelectors` inspect only protocol selector positions across query, mutation, batch, transact, search, clone, pull, push, and reconcile; application records and filter operands are ignored. - Selectors are normalized, deduplicated, and returned with the protocol version; omitting `protocolVersion` defaults to `"1"`. - Fails closed on unknown actions (`DFQL_UNSUPPORTED`), malformed selectors (`DFQL_INVALID`), and unsupported protocol versions (`DATAFN_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION`). - Re-exports the API from `@datafn/server` and shares the action inventory via `DataFnAction`; parser and extractor share fixtures so a new envelope shape cannot be accepted by one without the other. - Documents the API as the supported security-sensitive integration point in the request-authz, production-checklist, multi-region gateway, and reference docs. Written for commit 4eb55d039f969a4b37913aacf88fc85285c43fea. Summary will update on new commits. DataFn now owns `isAncestorInactive` end-to-end: it is derived from schema structure rather than declared by consumers. Breaking change (no compat window, per ticket discussion — there are no DataFn consumers yet; Nucleum migration is TIDY-474). **Core** (`core/src/system-fields.ts`, `schema.ts`) - Every dependent endpoint of an `inheritsInactive: true` relation (`from` for `many-one`, `to` otherwise; `many-many` ignored) gets an injected field: ```ts { name: "isAncestorInactive", type: "boolean", required: true, nullable: false, default: false, readonly: true } ``` - Ownership is computed from raw relations *before* resource normalization (relations normalize after resources). - Declaring the field on an owning resource fails with new `SYSTEM_FIELD_COLLISION`; the old "relation.inheritsInactive requires resource to define isAncestorInactive" check is removed. - `findSystemFieldWrite(relations, resource, record)` / `resourceRequiresAncestorInactive` exported for engines. **Write rejection (not strip)** — consumer `insert|merge|replace` records containing `isAncestorInactive` on an owning resource fail with `DFQL_INVALID "Field is read-only: ..."` at: server `executeMutation`, server sync `push`, client `mutate()` payloads, and direct offline `handleOfflineMutation`. Capability readonly fields keep their existing strip behaviour; this field is intentionally separate. Internal propagation still writes via `adapter.update`. **Propagation** — `relations.ts` decides support from relation topology instead of "did the consumer declare the field". `resolveAncestorInactive` is now exported. **Types / codegen** — `DatafnResourceRecord` intersects new `DatafnSystemRecord` so owning resources infer `isAncestorInactive: boolean` (required); tests assert this with `expectTypeOf`. `codegen`/`drizzle-codegen` needed no changes: they emit `readonly isAncestorInactive: boolean;` and `boolean("is_ancestor_inactive").notNull().default(false)` exactly once from the normalized schema (tests added). **Backfill** — new server export for existing rows (no CLI): ```ts recomputeAncestorInactive(adapter, schema, { namespace, batchSize?, cursor?, dryRun? }) -> { scanned, updated, nextCursor: { resource, afterId } | null } recomputeAncestorInactiveAll(adapter, schema, { namespace, ..., maxSweeps? }) // sweeps until no updates ``` Deterministic (`id` asc per sorted owning resource), idempotent, only writes when the stored value differs. ## Verification - `core`/`client`/`cli` full vitest suites and `core`/`server`/`client` typechecks pass; `core` lint clean (server/client/cli have no lint script). - `server` suite: 1032 pass; the 2 failures in `merge-sql-regression.test.ts` are `better-sqlite3` native bindings missing in this env (`npm install --ignore-scripts`), unrelated to this change. - Existing fixtures that declared `isAncestorInactive` (`ancestor-inactive.test.ts`, `local-dfql.test.ts`, `relation-counts-signal.test.ts`) had only that declaration removed, as required by the new collision rule. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/3f3e2978c22c4b559b7cf1effa79476e Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/3f3e2978c22c4b559b7cf1effa79476e?variant=devin Requested by: @thyaravind ## Summary by Sourcery Make `isAncestorInactive` a relation-derived DataFn system field maintained end-to-end by the runtime. New Features: - Derive and inject the required readonly `isAncestorInactive` system field from `inheritsInactive` relation topology. - Provide resumable and converging server backfill utilities for recomputing inherited inactivity on existing records. Bug Fixes: - Prevent consumer mutations from writing runtime-owned `isAncestorInactive` values while preserving internal propagation. - Align propagation, offline behavior, generated schemas, and inferred record types with relation-derived field ownership. Enhancements: - Add system-field collision validation and exported helpers for ownership and write detection. - Add type, code-generation, client, offline, server, and migration coverage for the new system-field behavior. Tests: - Expand automated coverage for schema injection, readonly write rejection, propagation, type inference, code generation, and backfill convergence. --- ## Summary by cubic Closes [DATA-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/DATA-3/own-isancestorinactive-as-a-datafn-system-field). Previously, consumers declared `isAncestorInactive`; DataFn now injects it as a required, readonly, default-false system field on dependent endpoints of `inheritsInactive` relations. Consumer declarations and `insert`/`merge`/`replace` writes on owning resources now fail, with no compatibility window. **Migration** - Remove existing declarations and run the exported `recomputeAncestorInactive` or `recomputeAncestorInactiveAll` backfill for stored records; it conditionally updates differing values, skips rows changed concurrently—including legacy null or absent values—and reports whether it converged within `maxSweeps`. - Propagation, generated schemas, and `DatafnResourceRecord` types now derive ownership from relation topology; offline propagation runs only on owning resources, and `many-many` relations remain unaffected. Written for commit d831914db5d2d62a776db817a2e64947adb46698. Summary will update on new commits. item.formatted_output: {"baseRefOid":"8e2c14350aefdedaf4288f0f589c3bb8a4d416af","body":"## Summary Closes [DATA-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/DATA-3/own-isancestorinactive-as-a-datafn-system-field). DataFn now owns `isAncestorInactive` end-to-end: it is derived from schema structure rather than declared by consumers. Breaking change (no compat window, per ticket discussion — there are no DataFn consumers yet; Nucleum migration is TIDY-474). **Core** (`core/src/system-fields.ts`, `schema.ts`) - Every dependent endpoint of an `inheritsInactive: true` relation (`from` for `many-one`, `to` otherwise; `many-many` ignored) gets an injected field: ```ts { name: "isAncestorInactive", type: "boolean", required: true, nullable: false, default: false, readonly: true } ``` - Ownership is computed from raw relations *before* resource normalization (relations normalize after resources). - Declaring the field on an owning resource fails with new `SYSTEM_FIELD_COLLISION`; the old "relation.inheritsInactive requires resource to define isAncestorInactive" check is removed. - `findSystemFieldWrite(relations, resource, record)` / `resourceRequiresAncestorInactive` exported for engines. **Write rejection (not strip)** — consumer `insert|merge|replace` records containing `isAncestorInactive` on an owning resource fail with `DFQL_INVALID "Field is read-only: ..."` at: server `executeMutation`, server sync `push`, client `mutate()` payloads, and direct offline `handleOfflineMutation`. Capability readonly fields keep their existing strip behaviour; this field is intentionally separate. Internal propagation still writes via `adapter.update`. **Propagation** — `relations.ts` decides support from relation topology instead of "did the consumer declare the field". `resolveAncestorInactive` is now exported. **Types / codegen** — `DatafnResourceRecord` intersects new `DatafnSystemRecord` so owning resources infer `isAncestorInactive: boolean` (required); tests assert this with `expectTypeOf`. `codegen`/`drizzle-codegen` needed no changes: they emit `readonly isAncestorInactive: boolean;` and `boolean("is_ancestor_inactive").notNull().default(false)` exactly once from the normalized schema (tests added). **Backfill** — new server export for existing rows (no CLI): ```ts recomputeAncestorInactive(adapter, schema, { namespace, batchSize?, cursor?, dryRun? }) -> { scanned, updated, nextCursor: { resource, afterId } | null } recomputeAncestorInactiveAll(adapter, schema, { namespace, ..., maxSweeps? }) // sweeps until no updates ``` Deterministic (`id` asc per sorted owning resource), idempotent, only writes when the stored value differs. ## Verification - `core`/`client`/`cli` full vitest suites and `core`/`server`/`client` typechecks pass; `core` lint clean (server/client/cli have no lint script). - `server` suite: 1032 pass; the 2 failures in `merge-sql-regression.test.ts` are `better-sqlite3` native bindings missing in this env (`npm install --ignore-scripts`), unrelated to this change. - Existing fixtures that declared `isAncestorInactive` (`ancestor-inactive.test.ts`, `local-dfql.test.ts`, `relation-counts-signal.test.ts`) had only that declaration removed, as required by the new collision rule. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/3f3e2978c22c4b559b7cf1effa79476e Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/3f3e2978c22c4b559b7cf1effa79476e?variant=devin Requested by: @thyaravind ## Summary by Sourcery Make `isAncestorInactive` a relation-derived DataFn system field maintained end-to-end by the runtime. New Features: - Derive and inject the required readonly `isAncestorInactive` system field from `inheritsInactive` relation topology. - Provide resumable and converging server backfill utilities for recomputing inherited inactivity on existing records. Bug Fixes: - Prevent consumer mutations from writing runtime-owned `isAncestorInactive` values while preserving internal propagation. - Align propagation, offline behavior, generated schemas, and inferred record types with relation-derived field ownership. Enhancements: - Add system-field collision validation and exported helpers for ownership and write detection. - Add type, code-generation, client, offline, server, and migration coverage for the new system-field behavior. Tests: - Expand automated coverage for schema injection, readonly write rejection, propagation, type inference, code generation, and backfill convergence. --- ## Summary by cubic Closes [DATA-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/DATA-3/own-isancestorinactive-as-a-datafn-system-field). Previously, consumers declared `isAncestorInactive`; DataFn now injects it as a required, readonly, default-false system field on dependent endpoints of `inheritsInactive` relations. Consumer declarations and `insert`/`merge`/`replace` writes on owning resources now fail, with no compatibility window. **Migration** - Remove existing declarations and run the exported `recomputeAncestorInactive` or `recomputeAncestorInactiveAll` backfill for stored records; it conditionally updates differing values, skips rows changed concurrently—including legacy null or absent values—and reports whether it converged within `maxSweeps`. - Propagation, generated schemas, and `DatafnResourceRecord` types now derive ownership from relation topology; offline propagation runs only on owning resources, and `many-many` relations remain unaffected. Written for commit d831914db5d2d62a776db817a2e64947adb46698. Summary will update on new commits. Rolling upgrades must negotiate manifest version `1` or refuse the operation. New DataFn internal namespace tables are represented by the contract and fail closed if missing from it. ## Summary by Sourcery Expose a versioned, fail-closed namespace storage contract and PostgreSQL planning APIs for safely operating on complete DataFn tenant storage. New Features: - Add a versioned namespace storage manifest exposing DataFn-owned logical roles, selector semantics, presence, ordering, and operation participation. - Provide PostgreSQL namespace storage inspection, plan resolution, operation selection, application-table composition, and permission-directory outbox draining APIs. Bug Fixes: - Fail closed when namespace storage versions, required relations or selector columns are unsupported, incomplete, unknown, invalid, or conflicting. Enhancements: - Separate outbox draining from ordinary copy, verification, cleanup, fencing, and backup responsibilities while preserving deterministic operation ordering. Documentation: - Document the namespace storage contract as the supported integration point for migration, backup, residency, fencing, outbox draining, and ownership tooling. Tests: - Add coverage for manifest integrity, deterministic plans, fail-closed validation, application storage composition, PostgreSQL catalog mapping, identifier validation, and namespace-scoped outbox draining. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a versioned namespace storage manifest and PostgreSQL plan resolver so consumers can build tenant copy, verify, cleanup, fence, drain, and backup plans without catalog heuristics or hard-coded `__datafn_*` names. This is the supported integration point for DATA-5; the API is additive, and rolling upgrades must negotiate manifest version `1` or refuse the operation. **New Features** - `@datafn/core` publishes `DATAFN_NAMESPACE_STORAGE_MANIFEST` with logical roles, selector kinds, presence, copy order, and operation participation. - `@datafn/server` adds `resolveNamespaceStoragePlan`, `inspectPostgresNamespaceStorage`, `selectNamespaceStorageEntries`, and `composeNamespaceStoragePlan` for application-owned tables. - Drain applies only to the permission-directory outbox; copy, verify, cleanup, fence, and backup are separate and deterministic. - Plan creation fails closed on unknown internal tables, missing selector columns, and unsupported manifest or schema versions. Written for commit 2e3f1f1622d82f5fded6eaff782542c2f21b19d3. Summary will update on new commits. item.aggregated_output: {"baseRefOid":"f6a2b03ee97f227e0db270c3b929b8bd0695cef8","body":"## Linear [DATA-5 — Expose canonical namespace storage metadata for DataFn operations](https://linear.app/21n/issue/DATA-5/expose-canonical-namespace-storage-metadata-for-datafn-operations) ## Summary - Add a versioned logical manifest in `@datafn/core` (`DATAFN_NAMESPACE_STORAGE_MANIFEST`) describing namespace storage roles, selector kinds (`resource_ns` vs `internal_namespace`), presence, copy order, and operation participation (`copy`, `verify`, `cleanup`, `fence`, `drain`, `backup`). - Add `@datafn/server` `resolveNamespaceStoragePlan` / `inspectPostgresNamespaceStorage` so consumers can build a complete tenant-scoped PostgreSQL plan without catalog heuristics or hard-coded `__datafn_*` names. - Distinguish drain (permission-directory outbox only) from copy/checksum/cleanup/fence/backup; fail closed on unknown internal tables, missing selector columns, and unsupported manifest/schema versions. - Allow composing application-owned tables without claiming DataFn ownership. - Document the API as the supported integration point for migration, backup, fencing, and physical-ownership tooling. - Skillplane placement/topology is unchanged; Skillplane can switch to this API after the DataFn release. ## Verification - `@datafn/core` typecheck and tests: 353 passed - `@datafn/server` typecheck - `@datafn/server` `src/namespace-storage.test.ts`: 17 passed - `@datafn/server` `src/execution/mutation/__tests__/share-spv2.test.ts`: 40 passed - No live PostgreSQL in this environment; catalog mapping is covered by `inspectPostgresNamespaceStorage` plus a synthetic installed-schema fixture ## Rollout notes The API is additive. Rolling upgrades must negotiate manifest version `1` or refuse the operation. New DataFn internal namespace tables are represented by the contract and fail closed if missing from it. ## Summary by Sourcery Expose a versioned, fail-closed namespace storage contract and PostgreSQL planning APIs for safely operating on complete DataFn tenant storage. New Features: - Add a versioned namespace storage manifest exposing DataFn-owned logical roles, selector semantics, presence, ordering, and operation participation. - Provide PostgreSQL namespace storage inspection, plan resolution, operation selection, application-table composition, and permission-directory outbox draining APIs. Bug Fixes: - Fail closed when namespace storage versions, required relations or selector columns are unsupported, incomplete, unknown, invalid, or conflicting. Enhancements: - Separate outbox draining from ordinary copy, verification, cleanup, fencing, and backup responsibilities while preserving deterministic operation ordering. Documentation: - Document the namespace storage contract as the supported integration point for migration, backup, residency, fencing, outbox draining, and ownership tooling. Tests: - Add coverage for manifest integrity, deterministic plans, fail-closed validation, application storage composition, PostgreSQL catalog mapping, identifier validation, and namespace-scoped outbox draining. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds a versioned namespace storage manifest and PostgreSQL plan resolver so consumers can build tenant copy, verify, cleanup, fence, drain, and backup plans without catalog heuristics or hard-coded `__datafn_*` names. This is the supported integration point for DATA-5; the API is additive, and rolling upgrades must negotiate manifest version `1` or refuse the operation. **New Features** - `@datafn/core` publishes `DATAFN_NAMESPACE_STORAGE_MANIFEST` with logical roles, selector kinds, presence, copy order, and operation participation. - `@datafn/server` adds `resolveNamespaceStoragePlan`, `inspectPostgresNamespaceStorage`, `selectNamespaceStorageEntries`, and `composeNamespaceStoragePlan` for application-owned tables. - Drain applies only to the permission-directory outbox; copy, verify, cleanup, fence, and backup are separate and deterministic. - Plan creation fails closed on unknown internal tables, missing selector columns, and unsupported manifest or schema versions. Written for commit 2e3f1f1622d82f5fded6eaff782542c2f21b19d3. Summary will update on new commits. The 16-package stable DAG is unchanged. The preset domain lives in `@uifn/registry` and is exported as `@uifn/registry/preset` (browser-safe). `@uifn/create` is private tooling only. ### Preset contract - Documented `UIFnPresetV1` with owned defaults, fail-closed unknown fields/versions, and deterministic `uifn1_` codes. - Axes: style, base color, theme, chart palette, fonts, icons, radius, density, menu treatment, framework, install mode. - Codes round-trip through encode/decode, share URLs, CLI, and `.uifn/preset.json` project resolution. ### Approved V1 mutation matrix - Template: `react-vite` - Framework: `react` - Package manager: `npm` - Install modes: `package`, `source` - Partial apply: `theme`, `font` Svelte/Solid remain valid encoded values so a shared visual preset can be reopened later. `uifn init` / `uifn apply` reject them with `UIFN_PRESET_UNSUPPORTED_COMBINATION`. ### CLI ```bash uifn preset encode|decode|resolve|url|open|tokens uifn init --preset [--dir] [--template react-vite] [--dry-run] uifn apply --preset [--only theme,font] [--dry-run] ``` Reapplying an identical preset is a no-op. Consumer-modified managed files return `UIFN_REGISTRY_DIRTY_CONFLICT`. Interrupted writes roll back. Source-mode init merges registry `package.json` dependencies into the scaffold so the transaction does not collide. ### Editor `uifn/create` generates every control from `PRESET_AXES`. Preview, generated project CSS, and token export use public `--uifn-*` variables only (no catalog-only component CSS). Light/dark, viewports, axis locks, and randomize unlocked are included. ## Out of this slice - Hosted `uifn.dev/create` deployment - Svelte/Solid/monorepo adapters - Screenshot visual baselines and hosted gallery - Previewing live `@uifn/components-react` package instances instead of token-painted fixtures (same fixture markup is used by editor and `init` so they match each other) - Exhaustive Cartesian option coverage (pairwise is implemented and tested) ## Verification - `@uifn/registry` typecheck passed - `@uifn/registry` tests: 41 passed, including 14 new preset contract/CLI tests (encode/decode/URL, pairwise, init/apply idempotence, partial theme/font, dirty conflict, interrupted rollback, svelte rejection, source-install dry-run + commit) - `@uifn/create` tests: 2 passed; typecheck passed ## Rollout notes Additive. No catalog resigning. No new public package. V1 codes become a compatibility contract; adding a field requires a new schema version and prefix. ## Summary by Sourcery Introduce versioned uifn presets and connect them to a safe project initialization, application, and visual editing workflow. New Features: - Add a versioned, shareable UIFnPresetV1 contract with deterministic encoding, URL support, validation, token compilation, and pairwise preset generation. - Add a private schema-driven uifn Create editor with preset controls, previews, responsive viewports, light/dark modes, locking, randomization, and exportable commands and tokens. - Add CLI preset encode/decode/resolve/url/open/tokens commands plus preset-driven project init and apply workflows for the approved React Vite matrix. Bug Fixes: - Prevent preset application from overwriting consumer-modified managed files and restore project state after interrupted transactions. Enhancements: - Reuse registry planning and transaction machinery for idempotent preset application, partial theme/font updates, project resolution, and source-install dependency merging. - Expose the browser-safe preset API from @uifn/registry/preset and document the V1 compatibility contract and supported mutation matrix. Build: - Add build and package exports for the registry preset module and introduce the private @uifn/create Vite workspace. Documentation: - Document the UIFnPresetV1 encoding, axes, compatibility rules, commands, and supported project workflows. - Document the private Create editor and shared preset URL format. Tests: - Add coverage for preset encoding, decoding, URL round trips, validation, pairwise combinations, editor integration, init/apply idempotence, partial application, dirty conflicts, rollback, framework rejection, and source-install dry runs. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds the first vertical slice of uifn Create: versioned `UIFnPresetV1` codes, a schema-driven visual editor, and safe project `init`/`apply` workflows. Preset logic lives in the new `@uifn/registry/preset` entrypoint and reuses the existing transaction, dirty-conflict, and rollback machinery. **Preset contract and CLI** - Codes are deterministic, self-contained, and fail closed on unknown fields, options, or future versions. - New `uifn preset encode|decode|resolve|url|open|tokens` commands; `uifn init --preset` and `uifn apply --preset` handle project mutation. - `init`/`apply` support the `react-vite`/`react`/`npm` matrix with `package` or `source` install modes and partial `theme`/`font` apply. - Svelte and Solid values remain decodable but are rejected with `UIFN_PRESET_UNSUPPORTED_COMBINATION` until those adapters are approved. **Editor and project safety** - `@uifn/create` is a private, schema-driven editor whose controls derive from `PRESET_AXES` and whose preview paints only public `--uifn-*` variables. - Reapplying an identical preset is a no-op; consumer-modified files return `UIFN_REGISTRY_DIRTY_CONFLICT` and interrupted writes roll back. Written for commit 6886076a5c34a766a249aa439041752d1a92b133. Summary will update on new commits. The 16-package stable DAG is unchanged. The preset domain lives in `@uifn/registry` and is exported as `@uifn/registry/preset` (browser-safe). `@uifn/create` is private tooling only. ### Preset contract - Documented `UIFnPresetV1` with owned defaults, fail-closed unknown fields/versions, and deterministic `uifn1_` codes. - Axes: style, base color, theme, chart palette, fonts, icons, radius, density, menu treatment, framework, install mode. - Codes round-trip through encode/decode, share URLs, CLI, and `.uifn/preset.json` project resolution. ### Approved V1 mutation matrix - Template: `react-vite` - Framework: `react` - Package manager: `npm` - Install modes: `package`, `source` - Partial apply: `theme`, `font` Svelte/Solid remain valid encoded values so a shared visual preset can be reopened later. `uifn init` / `uifn apply` reject them with `UIFN_PRESET_UNSUPPORTED_COMBINATION`. ### CLI ```bash uifn preset encode|decode|resolve|url|open|tokens uifn init --preset [--dir] [--template react-vite] [--dry-run] uifn apply --preset [--only theme,font] [--dry-run] ``` Reapplying an identical preset is a no-op. Consumer-modified managed files return `UIFN_REGISTRY_DIRTY_CONFLICT`. Interrupted writes roll back. Source-mode init merges registry `package.json` dependencies into the scaffold so the transaction does not collide. ### Editor `uifn/create` generates every control from `PRESET_AXES`. Preview, generated project CSS, and token export use public `--uifn-*` variables only (no catalog-only component CSS). Light/dark, viewports, axis locks, and randomize unlocked are included. ## Out of this slice - Hosted `uifn.dev/create` deployment - Svelte/Solid/monorepo adapters - Screenshot visual baselines and hosted gallery - Previewing live `@uifn/components-react` package instances instead of token-painted fixtures (same fixture markup is used by editor and `init` so they match each other) - Exhaustive Cartesian option coverage (pairwise is implemented and tested) ## Verification - `@uifn/registry` typecheck passed - `@uifn/registry` tests: 41 passed, including 14 new preset contract/CLI tests (encode/decode/URL, pairwise, init/apply idempotence, partial theme/font, dirty conflict, interrupted rollback, svelte rejection, source-install dry-run + commit) - `@uifn/create` tests: 2 passed; typecheck passed ## Rollout notes Additive. No catalog resigning. No new public package. V1 codes become a compatibility contract; adding a field requires a new schema version and prefix. ## Summary by Sourcery Introduce versioned uifn presets and connect them to a safe project initialization, application, and visual editing workflow. New Features: - Add a versioned, shareable UIFnPresetV1 contract with deterministic encoding, URL support, validation, token compilation, and pairwise preset generation. - Add a private schema-driven uifn Create editor with preset controls, previews, responsive viewports, light/dark modes, locking, randomization, and exportable commands and tokens. - Add CLI preset encode/decode/resolve/url/open/tokens commands plus preset-driven project init and apply workflows for the approved React Vite matrix. Bug Fixes: - Prevent preset application from overwriting consumer-modified managed files and restore project state after interrupted transactions. Enhancements: - Reuse registry planning and transaction machinery for idempotent preset application, partial theme/font updates, project resolution, and source-install dependency merging. - Expose the browser-safe preset API from @uifn/registry/preset and document the V1 compatibility contract and supported mutation matrix. Build: - Add build and package exports for the registry preset module and introduce the private @uifn/create Vite workspace. Documentation: - Document the UIFnPresetV1 encoding, axes, compatibility rules, commands, and supported project workflows. - Document the private Create editor and shared preset URL format. Tests: - Add coverage for preset encoding, decoding, URL round trips, validation, pairwise combinations, editor integration, init/apply idempotence, partial application, dirty conflicts, rollback, framework rejection, and source-install dry runs. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds the first vertical slice of uifn Create: versioned `UIFnPresetV1` codes, a schema-driven visual editor, and safe project `init`/`apply` workflows. Preset logic lives in the new `@uifn/registry/preset` entrypoint and reuses the existing transaction, dirty-conflict, and rollback machinery. **Preset contract and CLI** - Codes are deterministic, self-contained, and fail closed on unknown fields, options, or future versions. - New `uifn preset encode|decode|resolve|url|open|tokens` commands; `uifn init --preset` and `uifn apply --preset` handle project mutation. - `init`/`apply` support the `react-vite`/`react`/`npm` matrix with `package` or `source` install modes and partial `theme`/`font` apply. - Svelte and Solid values remain decodable but are rejected with `UIFN_PRESET_UNSUPPORTED_COMBINATION` until those adapters are approved. **Editor and project safety** - `@uifn/create` is a private, schema-driven editor whose controls derive from `PRESET_AXES` and whose preview paints only public `--uifn-*` variables. - Reapplying an identical preset is a no-op; consumer-modified files return `UIFN_REGISTRY_DIRTY_CONFLICT` and interrupted writes roll back. Nucleum should map the opaque subject to product user-home placement, select DataFn cells from server-owned config, and mint DataFn tickets itself. Already-issued signed assertions remain verifiable until `expiresAt` (default 60s, max 300s); new grants fail immediately after revoke, logout, deletion, or placement change. Python parity is included. This PR does not implement Nucleum deployment code or DataFn ticket minting. ## Summary by Sourcery Expose an opt-in, provider-neutral placement-bound authentication context for trusted regional data-plane consumers while preserving existing AuthFn routing and public behavior. New Features: - Add opt-in TypeScript and Python APIs for deriving immutable, placement-bound authentication context from valid sessions and user-owned API keys. - Support short-lived, audience-bound signed assertions for trusted private-service consumers. - Expose opaque subjects, placement epochs, authentication assurance, scopes, session bindings, and lifecycle timestamps without revealing sensitive identifiers or cell destinations. Bug Fixes: - Fail closed when credentials, identities, placements, or placement-directory access are invalid, revoked, expired, deleted, moving, tombstoned, missing, or unavailable. - Prevent client-controlled routing metadata and stale session handling from influencing derived placement context. Enhancements: - Add placement-context verification errors and observability events with privacy-preserving correlation and redaction. - Avoid refreshing sessions during context derivation and support issuer-controlled clocks, credential expiry, key rotation, and canonical authority validation. Build: - Add the Python idna dependency required for canonical authority handling. Documentation: - Document placement-bound context trust boundaries, integration guidance, revocation semantics, observability, and TypeScript/Python usage. Tests: - Add comprehensive TypeScript coverage for session, API-key, placement, assertion, audience, expiry, spoofing, and privacy behavior. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds an opt-in, placement-bound auth context API so trusted server-side code can derive regional routing context after a valid session or API key — previously downstream services had no non-spoofable way to learn a user's home region and placement epoch. **New Features** - TypeScript and Python issuer/verifier APIs (re-exported from `@authfn/multi-region`) return an immutable context (opaque subject, home region, placement epoch, canonical issuer, session/API-key binding, issued/expiry times, audience, scopes) that fails closed on invalid credentials, session, placement, or directory state. - Ignores client-supplied subject, region, epoch, issuer, and `x-authfn-routing-*` headers; omits raw email and identifiers. - Derivation never refreshes the session, evaluates expiry with the issuer's clock, supports async identity resolvers, and supports short-lived audience-bound HMAC assertions. - Adds `AUTHFN_PLACEMENT_CONTEXT_INVALID` and `authfn.placement_context.*` events routed through the configured observability sink; derivation and verification don't clone request bodies, and verification failures keep the originating request ID. - Python parity covers WHATWG origin canonicalization (IDNA, IPv4/IPv6, percent-encoded hosts, invalid ports), millisecond timestamps, UTC naive datetimes, lowercase auth schemes, nullable API-key misses, and empty or absent claim handling. **Migration** - The API is opt-in; public AuthFn routes and regional table ownership are unchanged until a consumer calls an issuer factory. - Nucleum should map the opaque subject to user-home placement, select DataFn cells from server-owned config, and mint DataFn tickets itself. - Signed assertions verify until `expiresAt` (default 60s, max 300s); new grants fail immediately after revoke, logout, deletion, or placement change. - Python consumers now require the `idna` dependency for WHATWG-compatible authority encoding. Written for commit a2685f21a2882bc3d9dad948325fa9ea18e37da5. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added opt-in placement-bound authentication contexts for trusted downstream services. - Contexts can be derived from authenticated sessions or API keys and optionally signed for verification across TypeScript and Python SDKs. - Added session revocation by session ID and optional session-state lookup without refreshing authentication timestamps in the Python SDK. - Added a dedicated 401 error for invalid placement contexts. - **Observability** - Added lifecycle events for issuance, rejection, verification, and verification failures. - **Documentation** - Added guides, recipes, reference entries, and security guidance for placement-bound contexts. item.formatted_output: {"baseRefOid":"f6a2b03ee97f227e0db270c3b929b8bd0695cef8","body":"## Linear [AUTH-2 — Expose placement-bound auth context for regional application data planes](https://linear.app/21n/issue/AUTH-2/expose-placement-bound-auth-context-for-regional-application-data) ## Summary - add an opt-in, provider-neutral AuthFn consumer API that derives placement-bound routing context only after a currently valid session succeeds - return an immutable context with opaque subject, home region, placement epoch, canonical issuer, session binding/version, issued/expiry times, audience, and assurance/scopes - ignore client-supplied subject, region, epoch, issuer, and `x-authfn-routing-*` headers; omit raw email/identifiers and cell destinations by default - fail closed for unauthenticated callers, revoked/expired sessions, deleted users, moving/deleting/tombstoned/missing placement, and directory unavailability - support in-process `derive` / `withContext` plus an optional short-lived audience-bound HMAC assertion for private service exchange - keep AuthFn tables regional and leave AUTH-1 canonical gateway plus legacy direct routing unchanged; AuthFn does not mint DataFn tickets or know DataFn URLs ## Verification - AuthFn core: 20/20 files; 108/108 tests, including 11 placement-context tests and 21 AUTH-1 gateway-routing tests - Python: 5/5 placement-context tests and 15/15 multi-region tests - `authfn` and `@authfn/multi-region` typecheck passed ## Rollout notes and limitations The API is disabled until a consumer opts in with `createAuthFnPlacementContextIssuer` / `create_placement_context_issuer`. Nucleum should map the opaque subject to product user-home placement, select DataFn cells from server-owned config, and mint DataFn tickets itself. Already-issued signed assertions remain verifiable until `expiresAt` (default 60s, max 300s); new grants fail immediately after revoke, logout, deletion, or placement change. Python parity is included. This PR does not implement Nucleum deployment code or DataFn ticket minting. ## Summary by Sourcery Expose an opt-in, provider-neutral placement-bound authentication context for trusted regional data-plane consumers while preserving existing AuthFn routing and public behavior. New Features: - Add opt-in TypeScript and Python APIs for deriving immutable, placement-bound authentication context from valid sessions and user-owned API keys. - Support short-lived, audience-bound signed assertions for trusted private-service consumers. - Expose opaque subjects, placement epochs, authentication assurance, scopes, session bindings, and lifecycle timestamps without revealing sensitive identifiers or cell destinations. Bug Fixes: - Fail closed when credentials, identities, placements, or placement-directory access are invalid, revoked, expired, deleted, moving, tombstoned, missing, or unavailable. - Prevent client-controlled routing metadata and stale session handling from influencing derived placement context. Enhancements: - Add placement-context verification errors and observability events with privacy-preserving correlation and redaction. - Avoid refreshing sessions during context derivation and support issuer-controlled clocks, credential expiry, key rotation, and canonical authority validation. Build: - Add the Python idna dependency required for canonical authority handling. Documentation: - Document placement-bound context trust boundaries, integration guidance, revocation semantics, observability, and TypeScript/Python usage. Tests: - Add comprehensive TypeScript coverage for session, API-key, placement, assertion, audience, expiry, spoofing, and privacy behavior. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds an opt-in, placement-bound auth context API so trusted server-side code can derive regional routing context after a valid session or API key — previously downstream services had no non-spoofable way to learn a user's home region and placement epoch. **New Features** - TypeScript and Python issuer/verifier APIs (re-exported from `@authfn/multi-region`) return an immutable context (opaque subject, home region, placement epoch, canonical issuer, session/API-key binding, issued/expiry times, audience, scopes) that fails closed on invalid credentials, session, placement, or directory state. - Ignores client-supplied subject, region, epoch, issuer, and `x-authfn-routing-*` headers; omits raw email and identifiers. - Derivation never refreshes the session, evaluates expiry with the issuer's clock, supports async identity resolvers, and supports short-lived audience-bound HMAC assertions. - Adds `AUTHFN_PLACEMENT_CONTEXT_INVALID` and `authfn.placement_context.*` events routed through the configured observability sink; derivation and verification don't clone request bodies, and verification failures keep the originating request ID. - Python parity covers WHATWG origin canonicalization (IDNA, IPv4/IPv6, percent-encoded hosts, invalid ports), millisecond timestamps, UTC naive datetimes, lowercase auth schemes, nullable API-key misses, and empty or absent claim handling. **Migration** - The API is opt-in; public AuthFn routes and regional table ownership are unchanged until a consumer calls an issuer factory. - Nucleum should map the opaque subject to user-home placement, select DataFn cells from server-owned config, and mint DataFn tickets itself. - Signed assertions verify until `expiresAt` (default 60s, max 300s); new grants fail immediately after revoke, logout, deletion, or placement change. - Python consumers now require the `idna` dependency for WHATWG-compatible authority encoding. Written for commit a2685f21a2882bc3d9dad948325fa9ea18e37da5. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added opt-in placement-bound authentication contexts for trusted downstream services. - Contexts can be derived from authenticated sessions or API keys and optionally signed for verification across TypeScript and Python SDKs. - Added session revocation by session ID and optional session-state lookup without refreshing authentication timestamps in the Python SDK. - Added a dedicated 401 error for invalid placement contexts. - **Observability** - Added lifecycle events for issuance, rejection, verification, and verification failures. - **Documentation** - Added guides, recipes, reference entries, and security guidance for placement-bound contexts. {"baseRefOid":"f6a2b03ee97f227e0db270c3b929b8bd0695cef8","body":" ## Summary Resolves [MCP-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-3/add-deterministic-client-profile-contracts-and-actionable-schema) by adding a deterministic authenticated client-profile contract to McpFn. McpFn already covered protocol conformance, manifests, semantic scenarios, and generic host capabilities. Those layers did not test the path from verified identity through `tools/list` projection and `tools/call` enrichment, and validation failures dropped the rejected property name. This change introduces a shared production lifecycle used by the runtime, testkit, and CLI: - Verified identity, protocol capabilities, and catalog behavior are distinct inputs. Profile selection never uses initialize `clientInfo`. - Catalog projection and trusted argument enrichment run before canonical schema validation. Generic clients keep the canonical catalog when no profile matches. - Server-owned required fields can be omitted from the model-visible schema and restored from trusted context. Model-provided values for those keys are overwritten. - Structured validation issues retain instance path, schema path, keyword, and the exact additional property. - `runClientProfileCompatibilitySuite()` and `mcpfn test-profiles` enumerate effective catalogs, check portability and projection/enrichment symmetry, run explicit fixtures through the production call path, and emit bounded redacted reports. Product identifiers, tenancy policy, and caller-attribution policy stay in the consumer. Protocol conformance and semantic scenarios remain separate gates. ## Testing - `npm test --workspace @mcpfn/core` — 82 tests, including new validation diagnostics and profile lifecycle coverage (unknown properties, enrichment, missing trusted context, forged server-owned metadata, initialize-metadata spoofing). - `npm test --workspace @mcpfn/testing` — 28 tests, including the compatibility suite, stale snapshots, asymmetry, and report redaction. - `npm test --workspace @mcpfn/cli` — 11 tests, including `mcpfn test-profiles`. - `npm run typecheck --workspace @mcpfn/core` ## Documentation `TESTING.md` now separates protocol conformance, deterministic profile compatibility, product scenarios, and live-client evidence. Architecture, requirements, test vectors, and package READMEs describe the same boundary. Linear Issue: [MCP-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-3/add-deterministic-client-profile-contracts-and-actionable-schema)
  
## Summary by Sourcery Introduce deterministic authenticated client-profile contracts and compatibility checks while improving actionable schema diagnostics. New Features: - Add authenticated client-profile contracts that resolve profiles from verified identity, project effective tool catalogs, and enrich server-owned call arguments before validation. - Add deterministic client-profile compatibility testing through the shared production lifecycle, including the `mcpfn test-profiles` CLI command and bounded redacted reports. Bug Fixes: - Preserve structured schema validation diagnostics, including instance paths, schema paths, keywords, missing properties, and rejected additional property names. Enhancements: - Keep generic clients on canonical catalogs and fail closed for profile ambiguity, version mismatches, missing trusted context, asymmetric projection and enrichment, and stale catalog snapshots. - Assess client-visible schemas for portability and prevent profile projectors from inventing tools. - Separate client-profile compatibility evidence from host capability checks, semantic scenarios, authentication testing, protocol conformance, and live-client evidence. Documentation: - Document the client-profile lifecycle, requirements, migration guidance, testing boundaries, compatibility vectors, and new CLI workflow. Tests: - Add core lifecycle, trusted-argument, profile resolution, schema portability, catalog diff, redaction, and validation diagnostic coverage. - Add testing-package compatibility-suite coverage for catalog enumeration, projection/enrichment symmetry, stale snapshots, captured failures, and report redaction. - Add CLI coverage for running client-profile compatibility checks. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds deterministic client-profile contracts and structured schema diagnostics to McpFn, resolving [MCP-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-3/add-deterministic-client-profile-contracts-and-actionable-schema). Previously, validation failures lost diagnostic detail and nothing tested the path from verified identity through `tools/list` projection and `tools/call` enrichment; the runtime, testkit, and CLI now share one production lifecycle for that path. **New Features** - Verified identity, protocol capabilities, and catalog behavior are distinct inputs; profile selection never uses initialize `clientInfo`. - Catalog projection and trusted argument enrichment run before canonical schema validation, and generic clients keep the canonical catalog when no profile matches. - Server-owned required fields can be omitted from the model-visible schema and restored from trusted context, with model-provided values overwritten. - `runClientProfileCompatibilitySuite()` and `mcpfn test-profiles` enumerate effective catalogs, check portability and projection/enrichment symmetry, and emit bounded redacted reports. - Product identifiers, tenancy policy, and caller-attribution policy stay in the consumer; protocol conformance and semantic scenarios remain separate gates. **Bug Fixes** - Validation issues now retain instance path, schema path, keyword, and the exact rejected additional property. Written for commit 44dc18b94c3f8b671a6956e9ad9a4ca61bb6cc01. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added verified client profiles that customize visible tool catalogs and securely restore server-managed input fields. * Added client-profile compatibility testing through the testing API and new `test-profiles` CLI command. * Added bounded, redacted compatibility reports with structured validation details. * **Documentation** * Documented client profiles, compatibility testing, migration guidance, lifecycle behavior, requirements, and test vectors. * Clarified compatibility report formats and distinctions between profile testing, conformance, scenarios, and live-client evidence. {"baseRefOid":"f6a2b03ee97f227e0db270c3b929b8bd0695cef8","body":" ## Summary Resolves [MCP-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-3/add-deterministic-client-profile-contracts-and-actionable-schema) by adding a deterministic authenticated client-profile contract to McpFn. McpFn already covered protocol conformance, manifests, semantic scenarios, and generic host capabilities. Those layers did not test the path from verified identity through `tools/list` projection and `tools/call` enrichment, and validation failures dropped the rejected property name. This change introduces a shared production lifecycle used by the runtime, testkit, and CLI: - Verified identity, protocol capabilities, and catalog behavior are distinct inputs. Profile selection never uses initialize `clientInfo`. - Catalog projection and trusted argument enrichment run before canonical schema validation. Generic clients keep the canonical catalog when no profile matches. - Server-owned required fields can be omitted from the model-visible schema and restored from trusted context. Model-provided values for those keys are overwritten. - Structured validation issues retain instance path, schema path, keyword, and the exact additional property. - `runClientProfileCompatibilitySuite()` and `mcpfn test-profiles` enumerate effective catalogs, check portability and projection/enrichment symmetry, run explicit fixtures through the production call path, and emit bounded redacted reports. Product identifiers, tenancy policy, and caller-attribution policy stay in the consumer. Protocol conformance and semantic scenarios remain separate gates. ## Testing - `npm test --workspace @mcpfn/core` — 82 tests, including new validation diagnostics and profile lifecycle coverage (unknown properties, enrichment, missing trusted context, forged server-owned metadata, initialize-metadata spoofing). - `npm test --workspace @mcpfn/testing` — 28 tests, including the compatibility suite, stale snapshots, asymmetry, and report redaction. - `npm test --workspace @mcpfn/cli` — 11 tests, including `mcpfn test-profiles`. - `npm run typecheck --workspace @mcpfn/core` ## Documentation `TESTING.md` now separates protocol conformance, deterministic profile compatibility, product scenarios, and live-client evidence. Architecture, requirements, test vectors, and package READMEs describe the same boundary. Linear Issue: [MCP-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-3/add-deterministic-client-profile-contracts-and-actionable-schema)
  
## Summary by Sourcery Introduce deterministic authenticated client-profile contracts and compatibility checks while improving actionable schema diagnostics. New Features: - Add authenticated client-profile contracts that resolve profiles from verified identity, project effective tool catalogs, and enrich server-owned call arguments before validation. - Add deterministic client-profile compatibility testing through the shared production lifecycle, including the `mcpfn test-profiles` CLI command and bounded redacted reports. Bug Fixes: - Preserve structured schema validation diagnostics, including instance paths, schema paths, keywords, missing properties, and rejected additional property names. Enhancements: - Keep generic clients on canonical catalogs and fail closed for profile ambiguity, version mismatches, missing trusted context, asymmetric projection and enrichment, and stale catalog snapshots. - Assess client-visible schemas for portability and prevent profile projectors from inventing tools. - Separate client-profile compatibility evidence from host capability checks, semantic scenarios, authentication testing, protocol conformance, and live-client evidence. Documentation: - Document the client-profile lifecycle, requirements, migration guidance, testing boundaries, compatibility vectors, and new CLI workflow. Tests: - Add core lifecycle, trusted-argument, profile resolution, schema portability, catalog diff, redaction, and validation diagnostic coverage. - Add testing-package compatibility-suite coverage for catalog enumeration, projection/enrichment symmetry, stale snapshots, captured failures, and report redaction. - Add CLI coverage for running client-profile compatibility checks. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds deterministic client-profile contracts and structured schema diagnostics to McpFn, resolving [MCP-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-3/add-deterministic-client-profile-contracts-and-actionable-schema). Previously, validation failures lost diagnostic detail and nothing tested the path from verified identity through `tools/list` projection and `tools/call` enrichment; the runtime, testkit, and CLI now share one production lifecycle for that path. **New Features** - Verified identity, protocol capabilities, and catalog behavior are distinct inputs; profile selection never uses initialize `clientInfo`. - Catalog projection and trusted argument enrichment run before canonical schema validation, and generic clients keep the canonical catalog when no profile matches. - Server-owned required fields can be omitted from the model-visible schema and restored from trusted context, with model-provided values overwritten. - `runClientProfileCompatibilitySuite()` and `mcpfn test-profiles` enumerate effective catalogs, check portability and projection/enrichment symmetry, and emit bounded redacted reports. - Product identifiers, tenancy policy, and caller-attribution policy stay in the consumer; protocol conformance and semantic scenarios remain separate gates. **Bug Fixes** - Validation issues now retain instance path, schema path, keyword, and the exact rejected additional property. Written for commit 44dc18b94c3f8b671a6956e9ad9a4ca61bb6cc01. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added verified client profiles that customize visible tool catalogs and securely restore server-managed input fields. * Added client-profile compatibility testing through the testing API and new `test-profiles` CLI command. * Added bounded, redacted compatibility reports with structured validation details. * **Documentation** * Documented client profiles, compatibility testing, migration guidance, lifecycle behavior, requirements, and test vectors. * Clarified compatibility report formats and distinctions between profile testing, conformance, scenarios, and live-client evidence. Bug Fixes: - Preserve structured schema validation diagnostics, including instance paths, schema paths, keywords, missing properties, and rejected additional property names. Enhancements: - Keep generic clients on canonical catalogs and fail closed for profile ambiguity, version mismatches, missing trusted context, asymmetric projection and enrichment, and stale catalog snapshots. - Assess client-visible schemas for portability and prevent profile projectors from inventing tools. - Separate client-profile compatibility evidence from host capability checks, semantic scenarios, authentication testing, protocol conformance, and live-client evidence. Documentation: - Document the client-profile lifecycle, requirements, migration guidance, testing boundaries, compatibility vectors, and new CLI workflow. Tests: - Add core lifecycle, trusted-argument, profile resolution, schema portability, catalog diff, redaction, and validation diagnostic coverage. - Add testing-package compatibility-suite coverage for catalog enumeration, projection/enrichment symmetry, stale snapshots, captured failures, and report redaction. - Add CLI coverage for running client-profile compatibility checks. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds deterministic client-profile contracts and structured schema diagnostics to McpFn, resolving [MCP-3](https://linear.app/21n/issue/MCP-3/add-deterministic-client-profile-contracts-and-actionable-schema). Previously, validation failures lost diagnostic detail and nothing tested the path from verified identity through `tools/list` projection and `tools/call` enrichment; the runtime, testkit, and CLI now share one production lifecycle for that path. **New Features** - Verified identity, protocol capabilities, and catalog behavior are distinct inputs; profile selection never uses initialize `clientInfo`. - Catalog projection and trusted argument enrichment run before canonical schema validation, and generic clients keep the canonical catalog when no profile matches. - Server-owned required fields can be omitted from the model-visible schema and restored from trusted context, with model-provided values overwritten. - `runClientProfileCompatibilitySuite()` and `mcpfn test-profiles` enumerate effective catalogs, check portability and projection/enrichment symmetry, and emit bounded redacted reports. - Product identifiers, tenancy policy, and caller-attribution policy stay in the consumer; protocol conformance and semantic scenarios remain separate gates. **Bug Fixes** - Validation issues now retain instance path, schema path, keyword, and the exact rejected additional property.
